<reason>Side B built the cleaner live route: flipping the default defeats veto-protected inertia, and sunsets create leverage to renew needed relief while stripping abuses. Side A's rubber-stamp-versus-cliff dilemma was sharp, but B split it by time and scope, while A's appropriations and repeal alternatives never overcame the one-third veto problem or zero-cost coercive decrees.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's response that defunding cannot stop costless coercion like protest bans or censorship, combined with the veto-math point that a 55-60% majority can still lose without a sunset, most decisively damaged Side A's alternatives.</best_rebuttal>
